topic: Resignation of Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka

en.dek: Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has resigned following court rulings that his education documents failed to meet election requirements, according to his aide.
body: Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned on 11 November 2026, according to his aide. The announcement came after weeks of legal scrutiny regarding the validity of the educational credentials he submitted during the election.

Court decisions issued in October 2026 prompted the vice-president's decision to step down. Both the Constitutional Court and the Supreme Court ruled last month that his education documents did not satisfy the legal requirements set for election candidates.

BBC reported on 11 November 2026 that Gibran's departure occurred alongside indications of strain within Indonesia's ruling political alliance. The news outlet cited the court decisions from the previous month as the immediate precursor to the vice-president stepping down.
CNA confirmed the resignation through Gibran's official aide on 11 November 2026. Neither the vice-president nor the presidential office has publicly named a successor to fill the vacant post.
facts: Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka submitted his resignation after court rulings on his education documents.
The Constitutional Court and Supreme Court ruled in October 2026 that his documents did not meet election requirements.
An aide to Gibran confirmed the resignation on 11 November 2026.
The resignation was reported by CNA and BBC on 11 November 2026.
en.title: Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigns over education documents
en.context: The Constitutional Court and Supreme Court issued separate rulings in October 2026 regarding the candidate requirements applied during the presidential election. Indonesian election law specifies minimum education standards for national candidates.
